newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin takes G7 break, meets corporate leaders.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin takes G7 break, meets corporate leaders.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, excluded from economic talks by Group of Seven leaders on Saturday, spent the time drumming up business for his country.
Yeltsin met corporate leaders from a dozen North American concerns, including Lockheed Martin Corp, which has already struck a $1 billion deal with Russia to buy rocket engines.

During the closed-door session, Yeltsin impressed the businessmen with his zeal for bilateral projects and his commitment to reforming the Russian tax code and solving troubling security issues, Lockheed Martin chairman Norman Augustine said.
"The president emphasized how much Russia wants to have American business in their country," he added.

Yeltsin himself moments earlier said Russia would meet all the obligations and deadlines of the rocket engine deal and the combination of U.S. and Russian technology would accomplish "amazing things".
"There should be no concern that Russia would be able to deliver," Yeltsin said.

Many Western firms have shunned Russia's often unpredictable economy and sluggish reform process, criticizing confusing and contradictory legislation and seemingly arbitrary decisions from senior officials.
But Augustine said Lockheed's eagerness to get its hands on "incredible" Russian engine technology outweighed those concerns.
"Clearly, they have a lot yet to accomplish," he said. "Sure, there are risks, but our experience to date has been that it's well worth the risk."
Lockheed last week announced it would spend more than $1billion on 101 engines to be built in Russia for use on its new Atlas rocket.
Russia has continued to develop new rocket engines, whereas U.S. firms have not built a new engine in some 25 years, Augustine noted.
The combination of advanced rocket technology with superior U.S. electronics will produce a far better engine than could have been built solely in the West, Augustine said.
"By bringing these technologies together, it has permitted Lockheed Martin to do things that we probably would never have been able to do otherwise," he added.
The deal came about without any cash subsidies from the U.S. government, Augustine added, though he conceded he did not remember just how the project actually got started.
Also meeting Yeltsin were officials from Amax Gold Inc, Agribusiness Partners International, United Technologies Corp, Cyprus Amax Minerals Co, Echo Bay Mines Ltd, Dupont Co, Newmont Gold Corp.
